faq.q: Why do different places have different times?
faq.a: Earth spins, so it is midday in one place while it is night somewhere else. Clocks follow the Sun, so they differ around the world.
asks: Why is it night in America when it's day in India?

faq.q: What happens if you fly all the way round the world?
faq.a: Going east, you move your watch forward in each time zone and gain 24 hours in total. Crossing the date line takes that day away again, so your calendar stays right.
asks: Do you gain a day flying round the world?

faq.q: Why is the date line in the Pacific Ocean?
faq.a: It sits opposite the Greenwich meridian, near 180 degrees, where there is mostly open sea. It zigzags around islands so no country is split into two dates.
asks: Where is the International Date Line?

faq.q: Why did Samoa skip a day in 2011?
faq.a: Samoa moved to the west side of the date line to share working days with Australia and New Zealand. So Thursday 29 December 2011 was followed by Saturday 31 December.

faq.q: Which place sees the New Year first?
faq.a: Kiribati's Line Islands, such as Kiritimati, are the first inhabited places, with Samoa and Tonga close behind.

facts: Earth turns 15 degrees every hour, so 24 one-hour zones go round the planet.
Samoa skipped Friday 30 December 2011 when it moved to the west side of the International Date Line.

quiz.say: You cross the International Date Line going west. What happens to the date?
quiz.show: You cross the International Date Line going west. What happens to the date?
quiz.why: Places west of the line are a day ahead, so the date jumps forward.

wrong.1: The date goes back a day when you cross going east.
wrong.2: The date line is exactly where the date changes.

quiz.say: How many degrees does Earth turn in one hour?
quiz.show: How many degrees does Earth turn in one hour?
quiz.why: 360 degrees divided by 24 hours is 15 degrees each hour.

wrong.1: 24 is the number of hours, not degrees per hour.
wrong.2: 60 is minutes in an hour, not degrees turned.
